scenarios.title: Needs and wants
scenarios.scenario: A city team has ₦5,000 to protect a community water point. A colourful banner would look exciting, but the water containers need replacing.

choices.label: Maintain essential water containers — ₦3,200
choices.consequence: The water point stays usable and ₦1,800 remains for other needs.
choices.tradeOff: The banner has to wait; the practical need is met first.

choices.label: Buy a welcome banner — ₦4,200
choices.consequence: Visitors see a banner, but the worn water containers still need attention.
choices.tradeOff: Only ₦800 remains for an urgent essential task.

scenarios.title: Opportunity cost
scenarios.scenario: A learning centre has ₦3,000 left. It can repair shared learning materials or pay for decorative signs.

choices.label: Restore learning materials — ₦1,500
choices.consequence: More learners can use the materials, and ₦1,500 stays available.
choices.tradeOff: Decorations are postponed in favour of everyday learning.

choices.label: Add decorative signs — ₦2,700
choices.consequence: The centre looks brighter but access to learning materials is unchanged.
choices.tradeOff: Only ₦300 is left to restore worn supplies.

scenarios.title: Budgeting in naira
scenarios.scenario: Your city team can spend at most ₦5,000 on a community learning day. Transport and basic supplies must both be considered.

choices.label: Transport ₦1,500 + supplies ₦3,000
choices.consequence: The essential trip and supplies are covered, with ₦500 held back.
choices.tradeOff: The refreshments would need to come from existing resources.

choices.label: Transport ₦3,000 + supplies ₦2,700
choices.consequence: The proposal exceeds the available money by ₦700.
choices.tradeOff: The team must reduce or defer a cost before acting.

scenarios.title: Saving and protecting resources
scenarios.scenario: A community has ₦2,500 for the week. Keeping a reserve could help with a later power interruption.

choices.label: Use ₦700 for maintenance and keep a reserve
choices.consequence: The community keeps ₦1,800 available for a later disruption.
choices.tradeOff: A decorative upgrade is delayed to protect future service.

choices.label: Use ₦2,300 on a one-day upgrade
choices.consequence: The visible upgrade is complete, but only ₦200 remains.
choices.tradeOff: A future urgent repair could be difficult to fund.

scenarios.title: The value of useful work
scenarios.scenario: The city has ₦1,500 to help more people understand a confusing process. Clarity matters more than advertising.

choices.label: Support a short skill demonstration — ₦200
choices.consequence: People learn a useful routine and ₦1,300 remains.
choices.tradeOff: The result depends on whether participants can actually use the skill.

choices.label: Pay for a poster campaign — ₦1,500
choices.consequence: Awareness increases, but nobody has tested whether the skill can be used.
choices.tradeOff: No resources remain for practical demonstrations.

scenarios.title: Honest value exchange
scenarios.scenario: Two contractors could improve a city marketplace. One gives accurate terms; another promises too much and cuts corners.

choices.label: Choose transparent and fair terms — ₦1,700
choices.consequence: The scope is honest and the city can inspect the outcome.
choices.tradeOff: There is less money for appearance, but the work is accountable.

choices.label: Choose an unrealistic cheap promise — ₦600
choices.consequence: The scope is unclear and the work may fail people who rely on it.
choices.tradeOff: The short-term saving introduces ethical and quality risks.

scenarios.title: Cash-flow basics
scenarios.scenario: The city workshop has ₦2,500 today. It must keep ₦1,800 for materials due before the next income arrives.

choices.label: Fund materials due now — ₦1,800
choices.consequence: The workshop covers the immediate obligation and retains ₦700.
choices.tradeOff: A new optional feature must wait until resources arrive.

choices.label: Start a non-urgent upgrade — ₦1,600
choices.consequence: Only ₦900 is available, leaving the ₦1,800 material bill unfunded.
choices.tradeOff: An attractive upgrade interrupts the working operation.

scenarios.title: Spotting suspicious offers
scenarios.scenario: A city supplier offers equipment at an unbelievable price and demands immediate secret payment.

choices.label: Pause and verify through known channels — ₦0
choices.consequence: The team avoids an unverified transaction while checking facts.
choices.tradeOff: The purchase is delayed; no one is pressured to send money.

choices.label: Send ₦4,500 immediately
choices.consequence: The city risks losing ₦4,500 to an unverified offer.
choices.tradeOff: Urgency and secrecy displaced careful verification.

scenarios.title: Borrowing decisions and risk
scenarios.scenario: A city group wants an expansion but cannot responsibly repay a proposed loan. It has ₦10,000 available for current work.

choices.label: Improve the small existing operation — ₦3,200
choices.consequence: The group protects essential work and keeps ₦6,800 available.
choices.tradeOff: Growth is slower, but no unsupported repayment promise is made.

choices.label: Commit ₦9,800 before reviewing repayment
choices.consequence: Almost all current resources are committed without a credible plan for later obligations.
choices.tradeOff: The expansion creates avoidable cash-flow and repayment risk.
